page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance utilizes the x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a substantial 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct performance profile. The instance delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its Geekbench single-core score of 2228.0, placing it in the top 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the strong top 25% tier. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, with stress-ng multi-core performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; both the Passmark memory score and uncached memory read/write bandwidth benchmarks are categorized in the bottom 25% tier.

Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core and lack of local storage, the c4n-highcpu-4 offers a specialized, cost-efficient profile for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing, text processing, and lightweight web serving. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive databases, heavy software compilation, or highly parallelized multi-threaded workloads due to its memory bandwidth constraints and lower multi-core benchmark scaling.
